newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY LEAGUE-BRITAIN HOLD OFF PNG FOR CLOSE WIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-BRITAIN HOLD OFF PNG FOR CLOSE WIN.

text.p: Britain on Saturday endured a
nail-biting finish to beat Papua New Guinea (PNG) 32-30 in a
rugby league test played in the PNG city of Lae.
PNG's Kumuls scored six tries to Britain's five and were on
course for an upset victory but for poor goal kicking by hooker
Elias Paiyo.
Paiyo could only kick three goals from six attempts while
Britain's Bobbie Goulding landed six from six to set up victory
for his side.
Britain started well in hot and humid conditions when Keiron
Cunningham scored in the third minute. Two errors by fullback
Stuart Spruce then allowed PNG to score twice.
A fine pass by Britain teenager Paul Sculthorpe set up a try
for Goulding before PNG re-established their lead with a try by
captain Adrian Lam just before halftime.
Lam was one of three PNG team members who played in the
Australian Rugby League competition this season, with the Kumuls
also coached by Australia's Bob Bennett.
Britain fought back in the second half with two tries by
Kris Radlinski and another by Anthony Sullivan to establish a
12-point buffer.
But PNG prop Ben Bire barged over for two tries and Robert
Sio scored another to bring PNG within two points and forced
Britain to endure a nervous final 90 seconds.
"Bobbie's kicking won us the match," Britain coach Phil
Larder told reporters.
"(PNG) are a very good team now and they had some excellent
players out there today, but fortunately not a kicker," he said.
